question: Point out the correct answer regarding B lymphocytes.

options.opa: Its two main subpopulations are called B-helper and B-cytotoxic.
options.opb: They are the cells responsible for the production of antibodies in the rejection of an autologous transplant of hematopoietic progenitors.
options.opc: They are the target cells of the anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody (rituximab).
options.opd: They require co-stimulation CD20-CD19 for the expression of the CD3 molecule on its surface.
options.ope: It is the type of majority lymphocyte in the peripheral blood of patients with Bruton's disease.

analysis: B lymphocytes are a type of white blood cell that plays a crucial role in the immune response by producing antibodies to fight off infections. They are not divided into B-helper and B-cytotoxic subpopulations. They are not responsible for rejecting autologous transplants, as they would not recognize self-tissues as foreign. B lymphocytes are indeed the target cells of the anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody rituximab, which is used in conditions like certain types of lymphoma and autoimmune diseases. B lymphocytes do not require co-stimulation of CD20-CD19 for the expression of the CD3 molecule on their surface. Patients with Bruton's disease, also known as X-linked agammaglobulinemia, have a deficiency in B lymphocytes, so they would not have a majority of B lymphocytes in their peripheral blood.
